video.title: Missed Every Gold Rush? This One Started Just 2 Days Ago

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Jacob Posel, an Australian AI builder in San Francisco, on the day OpenAI released its image generation API. They brainstorm consumer wrapper apps (Ghibli-style portraits, future-baby images, weight-loss visualiser, ageing), vertical uses (virtual staging, Airbnb photos, tree-trimming lead images) and, most deeply, AI ad creative: white-labelling high-volume ad variants for agencies or selling a $200/month tool to agencies via permissionless remade ads. Jacob shares reference-image prompting tips and says reliable viable-ad systems are still unsolved. Key takeaway: be ready to ship the moment a new capability drops, and target outputs that make customers money.

tactics.name: Reference-ad variant generation
steps: Screenshot a competitor's or your own winning ad as the reference
Tell the model clearly which image is the reference ad to reproduce and which is the product
Generate multiple variants (4 in Sora, 50 via API) and pick the best to refresh fatigued ads

quote.text: the reference image can be one the reference ad which is just a screenshot of the ad that you like and two can be your product
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

tactics.name: Piggyback on agencies with a white-label offer
steps: Offer to deliver AI ads under their brand to existing and dormant clients
Price per ad with markup, revenue split, or retainer plus per-ad-accepted
Deliver finished ads in Google Drive in the client's format

quote.text: I would literally send them Google Drive folders of just completed ads
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

tactics.name: Permissionless spec work for agencies
steps: Pick agencies not yet using AI
Remake several of a client's ads
Send them proactively with a link to your tool

quote.text: a lot of these ad agencies list out their customers, right? They just make it too easy for growth hackers like us
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine Sora Explore for app ideas
steps: Scroll Sora's explore page sorted by likes
Look at the exact prompts and former popular filters
Turn a top prompt into a focused wrapper

quote.text: I highly recommend anyone listening to this just scroll through Sora and just take a look at their explore page

warnings.warning: Without solving how to reliably produce viable ads you'll get a spike then massive churn.

quote.text: Otherwise, you're going to have a massive spike and a massive churn
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

warnings.warning: AI video is still a gimmick; not worth investing time yet.

quote.text: Videos still haven't had that moment we spoke about before. They're still unusable
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

warnings.warning: Getting customers to use tools themselves is hard; do it for them first.
Some image-enhancement uses (Airbnb photos) draw backlash as deceptive.
Spreading thin across opportunities means not winning at anything.

quote.text: when I get to spread thin, then I kind of don't really win at anything
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: New API releases create short gold rushes; prepare in advance and launch the day they drop.

quote.text: if you had been preparing for it, you you could have created like a really really great outcome for yourself starting today
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: Most people outside tech don't know what AI can do; packaging one capability into a focused app is the opportunity.
Image outputs tied to revenue (ads) are the best use because buyers see ROI.
Ad algorithms now reward creative volume and variety, so demand for cheap high-volume creative is rising.

quote.text: the ad algorithms are starting to reward volume and choice more than high focus
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: Reference images improve output far more than describing the image.

quote.text: that will improve the quality of the output like orders of magnitude more than if you were to try and describe that image
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: Agencies are arbitrage businesses and will resell any service they can mark up.

quote.text: if you can deliver the service to them and they can sell it for more, then they're going to say yes
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: Clients want predictable monthly costs; flat pricing or approval-based per-ad pricing avoids bill shock.

quote.text: usually brands want to know like what is this going to cost me per month?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: People look for excuses not to launch.

quote.text: People look for a million reasons not to do something
quote.speaker: Jacob Posel

lessons.lesson: Cheap creative enables hyper-targeted personas instead of a few broad ones.

evidence_quality.rationale: Speculative brainstorm on launch day; no revenue from any idea; Jacob has hands-on prompting experience but no business results stated.
